indicators.name: Taxa de mortalidade infantil (óbitos de menores de 1 ano por mil nascidos vivos)
indicators.officialSource: IBGE - Tábuas Completas de Mortalidade para o Brasil / Projeções da População
indicators.notes: Single source family: IBGE (not Ministério da Saúde/SIM-Sinasc, whose direct/corrected TMI differs, e.g. MS Boletim Epidemiológico gives 14.0 for 2016). 2006-2015 from IBGE Brasil em Síntese table (projection-based series, 2 decimals); 2016-2019 from the annual Tábuas Completas de Mortalidade releases, which are projections built from Census 2010 data and continue the same downward path. METHODOLOGY BREAKS: (1) 2020 and 2021 tábuas were pure projections that IBGE says do not incorporate COVID-19 effects; omitted. (2) The 2022 tábua (12.9) was built from Census 2022 population + death registrations with corrections, so 2019->2022 is not a like-for-like comparison. (3) 2023 (12.5) and 2024 (12.3) come from tábuas derived from Projeções da População Revisão 2024 (2000-2070), which revised the whole history; per Agência Brasil's reproduction of the revised series, 2000 = 28.1 and 2020 = 11.4 (not included here to avoid mixing vintages with 2006-2019). The revised 2024-projection series for 2006-2021 was not found in search results; when available, it should replace 2006-2022 for full consistency. 2025 tábua not yet released (IBGE usually publishes late November). Série dividida: anos a partir de 2022 (base Censo 2022 / projeção 2024) estão em mortalidade_infantil_censo2022, para não serem comparados com a série antiga.

indicators.name: Cobertura vacinal da tríplice viral, 1ª dose (SCR D1)
indicators.officialSource: Ministério da Saúde - SI-PNI / DataSUS (via estudos e comunicados que reproduzem os dados)
indicators.notes: Measure: MMR/tríplice viral first dose (D1), Brazil, % of target population (meta PNI 95%). PRIMARY DATA (DataSUS TabNet / IBGE séries estatísticas MS42) COULD NOT BE ACCESSED in this session (hosts blocked); values come from secondary reproductions of SI-PNI data. 2015-2021 from one source (Stocki et al., BJID 2026 congress abstract, SI-PNI data). 2022-2023 from Ministério da Saúde figures as reported by Afya/press. POSSIBLE VINTAGE BREAK between 2021 and 2022: SI-PNI coverage figures are revised retroactively (late registrations, denominator updates; from 2023 doses are drawn from RNDS), and the 2021 value here (71.4) is lower than other circulating figures. Treat 2021->2022 change with caution. Omitted: 2006-2014 (sources only say D1 was >=95% in all regions 2003-2014, no national annual numbers found), 2016, 2018; 2024 (preliminary 95.5-96% reported, MS said target 95% was exceeded, consolidated number not confirmed); 2025 (Ministry figure of ~92.7-92.9% reported in press, source attribution unclear). Recommend replacing the whole series with a single DataSUS TabNet extraction (Imunizações - Cobertura, Tríplice Viral D1, Brasil, 2006-2025).

indicators.name: IDEB - Anos iniciais do ensino fundamental (Brasil, total)
indicators.officialSource: INEP - Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica
indicators.notes: Biennial; national total (all networks: public + private). Public network differs (e.g. 5.7 in 2019/2023, 6.1 in 2025). 2021 edition was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic (school closures, automatic promotion policies inflated the flow/approval component; INEP flagged caution in interpreting 2021). Values from an INEP table reproduced in a PDF (Revista Cenarium) for 2005-2025; 2023->2025 (6.0 -> 6.3) confirmed by SBT News and Agência Gov. Ideb 2025 released 5 Aug 2026.

indicators.name: IDEB - Anos finais do ensino fundamental (Brasil, total)
indicators.officialSource: INEP - Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica
indicators.notes: Biennial; national total (all networks). Public network: 4.7 (2023) -> 5.0 (2025). 2007-2021 values taken from the Portuguese Wikipedia IDEB table (which reproduces INEP results but is a secondary source; the official INEP planilhas could not be opened in this session); 2005, 2023 and 2025 confirmed by press coverage of the INEP release. 2021 (5.1) is pandemic-affected: approval/flow component was inflated, so the 2021->2023 dip to 5.0 partly reflects that artefact rather than a real decline. Ideb 2025 released 5 Aug 2026.

indicators.name: Rendimento médio mensal real domiciliar per capita
indicators.officialSource: IBGE - PNAD Contínua, Rendimento de todas as fontes 2025
indicators.notes: Constant prices: average 2025 prices (reference year 2025), as published in the 'Rendimento de todas as fontes 2025' informativo (May 2026). 2025 = R$ 2,264, record of the series begun in 2012; +6.9% vs 2024 and +18.9% vs 2019. Only 2019, 2024 and 2025 were visible at 2025 prices in search results; 2012-2018 and 2020-2023 omitted (the full table is in the informativo / SIDRA but the host was blocked). Do NOT mix with: (a) the nominal 'rendimento domiciliar per capita' published for FPE purposes (R$ 2,316 in 2025; R$ 2,069 in 2024; R$ 1,893 in 2023; R$ 1,625 in 2022), which uses first visits and for 2020-2022 used the fifth visit; (b) the 2024 release's real value (R$ 2,020 at 2024 prices). Methodology note: for 2020-2022 IBGE used 5th-visit interviews instead of 1st-visit.

indicators.name: Taxa de investimento (FBCF / PIB)
indicators.officialSource: IBGE - Sistema de Contas Nacionais (referência 2010) e Contas Nacionais Trimestrais
indicators.notes: Current prices ratio. Each year uses the latest annual SCN (referência 2010) vintage found: 2010-2018 from the SCN 2018 indicator table; 2019 from SCN 2019 (Nov 2021); 2020 from SCN 2020 (Nov 2022); 2021 from SCN 2021 (Nov 2023); 2022 and 2023 from SCN 2023 (Nov 2025). 2024 and 2025 are from the Contas Nacionais Trimestrais (4th-quarter release, Mar 2026) and are preliminary (2024 was first published as 17.0, revised to 16.9). Earlier vintages differ materially (e.g. 2022 first published as 18.8, later 17.8; FGV/IBRE cites 19.2 for 2021 from quarterly data). IBGE is migrating the SCN to base 2021, which will revise the whole series. 2006-2009 OMITTED: only old-methodology figures were found (16.4 in 2006, 19.1 in 2008, 16.9 in 2009, pre-2015 series excluding R&D), not comparable with the referência-2010 series (which raised 2010 from 19.5/18.4 to 20.5-20.6).
